rationale: The independent warning and the targeted rejection identify the same false word, unitary, in the same explanatory sentence; the confirmed-fatal repair replaces it by normal.

The independent warning and targeted rejection identify the identical invariance sign error in step 1.1; the confirmed-fatal repair changes [H,f] to [f,H] and the resulting coefficient from negative to positive.

The independent warning and targeted rejection identify the same false negative-sign bracket formula and the same resulting wrong normalization of f; the confirmed-fatal repair derives the positive formula and selects the opposite scalar.

The independent warning and targeted rejection identify the same mishandled zero-dimensional case in step 1.1; the confirmed-fatal repair records the empty numerical range as convex and treats the one-dimensional singleton separately.

The independent warning and targeted rejection identify the same false negative sign in step 1.1; the confirmed-fatal repair derives the positive bracket coefficient from invariance and nondegeneracy.

The independent warning and targeted rejection identify the same beta+k alpha indexing error and the same false p=q=1 conclusion; the confirmed-fatal repair uses the indices -2,-1,0 and obtains p=2,q=0.

The warning's invalid F=G specialization lies in the same summability proof rejected for ordering complex sums. The confirmed-fatal repair replaces that argument and obtains the diameter bound from arbitrary tails containing F_0.

The warning identified the missing scalar-completeness input in the same item whose targeted rejection licensed repair. The repair now cites finite-dimensional real/complex Banach completeness before taking coordinate limits.

The Markdown source contains two correctly numbered claims and both renderable formulas; the lack of a separating newline after the first display is presentational only and does not alter or obscure either mathematical assertion enough to warrant a content edit at fatal-only Step 7.

The targeted rejection invalidated the example's explicit graft construction. Its confirmed-fatal re-authoring also removes the warning's unsupported same-level sibling assertion and derives nowhere density solely from the finite-union argument already proved in step 1.2.

The naturality clause is supported by functoriality of pair long exact sequences and the exact-couple construction, which is an immediate standard construction from the displayed maps; the later naturality theorem expands the same mechanism. The warning identifies terse exposition, not a false claim or uncloseable proof gap.

With the page's sphere-coordinate-first suspension convention and the connecting-map convention fixed in the pair exact sequence, the collapse map has the cellular incidence degree with no additional sign. The cited source diagram supplies this normalization; recomputing it locally would be useful polish but is not required to make the claim true.

The connective spectrum ku represents a reduced generalized cohomology theory, so the skeletal AHSS applies; the item's source assumptions and repaired comparison now state the required representability and coefficient-range comparison. The warning was a premise-explication gap a reader can close, not an independently fatal defect.

The item openly marks the Eilenberg-Mac Lane cohomology and Bott-cofiber computations as source inputs and gives precise source locators; its local argument only needs the resulting two-element dichotomy and normalization. Dependence on verified source computations is load-bearing but is not itself a content defect.

The equal-dimension criterion follows immediately by applying the cited Hilbert-space-to-ell-two isomorphism to bases with the same cardinality, while a unitary transports an orthonormal basis to one of the same cardinality. The warning identifies an assembled elementary consequence, not a false claim or a gap requiring content repair.

Fact [A4] cites an orthonormal-family definition rather than the exact Bessel theorem, but the asserted weak-null conclusion follows by the one-line Bessel estimate and is a reader-closeable citation-presentation gap. The item's targeted rejection concerned a different spectral-calculus supplier and did not license this presentation edit.

The fifteen references use the correct URL and numbered locators but give the PDF an inaccurate bibliographic title. That metadata mismatch is presentational and does not change the mathematical statements, source document, or locators; fatal-only Step 7 does not authorize content edits for it.

Given the orthogonal decompositions in [A1], the direct sum of the two stated surjective isometries is immediately a surjective isometry on H. The cited partial-isometry theorem is not the exact direct-sum statement, but the missing calculation is elementary and reader-closeable; the targeted rejection repaired a separate Cayley-transform inference.

The cited basis-existence and Hilbert-space-to-ell-two results assemble directly into the equal-basis-cardinality unitary criterion, and a unitary transports a basis in the converse direction. This is an elementary synthesis of the cited statements, not an independently fatal defect.

The statement transposed the unequal-length Cartan pairs: with |alpha| at least |beta|, the first denominator is larger, so the pairs are (1,2),(-1,-2) and (1,3),(-1,-3). This is a false statement, independently fatal from the targeted proof-step rejection, and was repaired in the same item edit.

The sentence contrasts the Hilbert adjoint with the Banach transpose after displaying their different source and target spaces and the exact Riesz-map conjugation formula. Calling them different operators is imprecise presentation, but the typed formula is correct and the definition is unaffected; fatal-only Step 7 does not authorize a content edit.

The theorem assumes Countable Choice even though its equivalence for a supplied point p is choice-free, and the proof explicitly says so. The stronger ambient hypothesis does not make either implication false or leave a proof gap, so this is nonfatal hypothesis presentation and receives no content edit at fatal-only Step 7.

The definition first constructs decomposition-dependent data and labels them as such, while the subsequent intertwiner lemma proves fiber-dimension invariance before the classification theorem uses the resulting invariant. The later theorem does not presuppose the independence it proves, so there is no circularity or defect.
